A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SeTGAP research. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable, including Appendices A–H in v1 and A–I in v2. Retained and relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original symbolic-regression experiments on 13 synthetic functions, noise and hyperparameter analyses, and four SRBench++ functions.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds SeTGAP experiments on a selected Feynman benchmark subset in Section 4.2 and Appendix I.

M1.justification: Sections 3.2.2–3.3.3 replace Pearson-correlation maximization with MSE minimization for univariate coefficient fitting, combined-skeleton evaluation, and variable ordering during cascade merging. This revises several central selection decisions, while retaining the transformer architecture and recursive merging procedure.

E1.justification: v2 retains the 13 synthetic functions and four SRBench++ functions and adds the Feynman physics-equation benchmark, filtered according to model expressivity. Section 4.2 describes 78 selected problems, substantially broadening equation and variable-interaction coverage; the detailed result tables contain 77 problem rows.

E2.justification: The original PySR, TaylorGP, NeSymReS, E2E, TPSR, and uDSR comparisons remain. The added Feynman comparison uses reported results from 14 additional comparators, including AIFeynman, AFP, AFP_FE, DSR, GP-GOMEA, Operon, and SBP-GP, verified in Figures 3–4 and Tables 45–48.

E3.justification: Section 4.2 introduces SRBench partition-based evaluation, benchmark eligibility filtering, symbolic-recovery and R² metrics, and aggregation across problems. The retained synthetic experiments preserve their sample sizes, extrapolation domains, noise levels, and search budgets. The PDFs do not establish that the retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Section 5 adds a focused Feynman case analysis, including recovered expressions for II.34.29a that illustrate coefficient error despite correct symbolic structure. Existing noise and hyperparameter analyses are retained. Appendix E is renamed from Hyperparameter Tuning to Ablation Studies without adding ablation experiments.

E5.justification: Beyond v1's repeated-run means, standard deviations, and Tukey tests, v2 introduces standard errors across benchmark problems and Kruskal–Wallis tests followed by Dunn comparisons with Holm correction for Feynman MSE. The new R² uncertainty reporting is inconsistent: Appendix I calls it standard error, whereas the table captions call it standard deviation.

E6.justification: The original synthetic, noise, hyperparameter, and SRBench++ results are retained. New Feynman results place SeTGAP second in symbolic recovery at approximately 61.2%, seventh in aggregated R², and fourth in aggregated MSE, as shown in Figures 3–4. Tables 45–48 add detailed per-problem results.

T1.justification: Section 3.2.2 changes the mathematical optimization problem defining the coefficient optimum from maximizing correlation to minimizing squared error. The SR problem definition, Proposition 1, its structural-induction proof in Appendix C, and the skeleton-equivalence identities remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion add a claim of high symbolic recovery with competitive predictive performance on Feynman problems. The central contributions concerning decomposable symbolic regression, preservation of skeleton structure, and noise robustness remain. Section 4.2 explicitly emphasizes interpretability rather than claiming state-of-the-art regression performance.

C2.justification: v2 removes the rationale for scale- and offset-invariant correlation selection. It adds benchmark-specific qualifications concerning separability, narrow input ranges, misleading aggregation across differently scaled problems, and coefficient precision versus structural recovery. The earlier computational-cost, dimensionality, and operator-complexity limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix A, Table 7 removes acos, asin, and atan from the documented pretraining vocabulary. Section 4.2 also identifies unsupported power operators used when selecting benchmark problems. These revise the documented capabilities; the PDFs do not establish retraining. Other architecture and hyperparameter details are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds references supporting the expanded benchmark comparison, including work on AFP, FFX, FEAT, ITEA, and GP-GOMEA. This broadens comparative positioning, while Section 2's related-work narrative and the substantive comparison with CVGP remain essentially unchanged.

P1.justification: The experimental section gains separate synthetic and benchmark subsections, Appendix I is added, and Appendix E is renamed. Objective descriptions and benchmark discussion receive localized revisions. Most of the introduction, related work, method exposition, and retained appendices remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figures 3–4 with three benchmark comparison panels, Table 44 listing Feynman equations, and Tables 45–48 presenting detailed results. These substantially expand the evidence displays. Earlier figure images are retained and renumbered, with additional repositioning of tables and algorithm blocks.

improvement.justification: The Feynman comparison supplies broader empirical support than v1's 13-function study and four SRBench++ cases, with useful qualifications about benchmark scope and predictive accuracy. However, Tables 45–48 omit II.11.7 from the stated 78-problem set, R² uncertainty labels conflict, and Algorithm 3 retains a maximum-score return after switching to MSE minimization. These reporting and specification inconsistencies limit the overall gain.
